texts.facts: Plaintiffs' case: 1. The facts of the case, in brief, as borne out from the record are that plaintiff No.1 claims itself to be an Authorized Representative of brand name "Ardh Sainik Canteen"; whereas, plaintiff No.2 is the proprietor of trademark "ARDH SAINIK CANTEEN" with requisite logo by virtue of Trademark Certificate dated 17.05.2022 in Class 35. As per the case set up in the matter, plaintiff No.1 claims itself to be a registered trust by the name of "Ardh Sainik Welfare Trust", created to facilitate the defence and/or Army personnel for their overall growth in their personal and social life. The plaintiffs are engaged in providing ready-to-work opportunities to the aforesaid defence personnel in various fields by having stores by the name of "Ardh Sainik Canteen" for providing and generating self-business schemes. The said stores keep Fast Moving Consumer Goods (in short FMCG) which are sold to the retired Army/Para-Military personnel. The plaintiffs have been operating since the year 2015 in the CS (Comm) No.184/2023: Ardh Sainik Canteen & Anr. V/s Bhhotpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen/ Ex.Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen: DOD: 28.10.2025 field and have opened more than 635 canteens across India. The plaintiffs got their trademark "ARDH SAINIK CANTEEN", registered with the Trade Mark Registry, vide Certificate No.2979886, details whereof for ready reference is tabulated hereunder: Trademark Application Class Certificat No No. 5188201 35 2979886 Ardh Sainik Canteen (Word Mark) 2. (i) It has been alleged that sometime in the year 2022, plaintiffs came to know through an advertisement that the defendant had been illegally and Ardh Sainik Canteen vs Bhhotpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen on 28 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7367288/ 2 unauthorizedly using the name of plaintiffs by running a canteen/outlet in the name and style of "BHHOTPURV ARDH SAINIK KALYAN CANTEEN/EX.ARDH SAINIK KALYAN CANTEEN/ ", at Heera Complex Wali Gali, Near Bajrang Hospital, Bijnor Road, Gauri Sarojini Nagar, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh-226008. (ii) On enquiries being made by the plaintiffs, it was found that the defendant had been functioning and running the store in a somewhat CS (Comm) No.184/2023: Ardh Sainik Canteen & Anr. V/s Bhhotpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen/ Ex.Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen: DOD: 28.10.2025 similar name of the plaintiff, targeting the same consumers fully knowing/getting aware that the plaintiffs had a chain of groceries store/ canteens by the name of "ARDH SAINIK CANTEEN". This led to issuance of legal notice dated 23.01.2023 by the plaintiffs to the defendant to cease and desist from the using the trademark of the plaintiffs for running its store. The said legal notice was correctly addressed to the defendant, to which reply was filed on behalf of defendant, inter alia denying the contents of legal notice and claiming that the use of name "Ardh Sainik Canteen" was nowhere violative of the trademark of plaintiffs, as the same was nowhere similar to that of plaintiff. The plaintiffs claim that on account of targeting their consumers by the defendant irreparable loss, agony and humiliation has been suffered by them. 3. As such, the plaintiffs filed the present suit against the defendant, inter alia praying as under: (i) A decree of permanent and mandatory injunction against the defendant, thereby restraining the defendant, his agent, representatives, legal heirs, assignees from illegally/unauthorizedly using the trademark and intellectual property of plaintiff(s), i.e name, style and mark in the name of "ARDH SAINIK CANTEEN"; and (ii) Costs of the suit. (a) On the other hand, defendant firm examined its proprietor namely Shri Prafullit Dixit as DW-1 in the matter, who in his evidence by way of Affidavit Ex.DW1/1 has reiterated the averments made in the written statement and proved on record the following documents: (i) Copy of his Aadhar Card as Ex.DW1/A (OSR); (ii) Copy of his PAN Card as Ex.DW1/B (OSR); (iii) Coloured photographs of the canteen run by defendant under CS (Comm) No.184/2023: Ardh Sainik Canteen & Anr. In case reported as, "(1972) 1 SCC 618", titled as, "Parle Products (P) Limited V/s J.P & Co., Mysore", the Hon'ble Supreme Court has been pleased to lay down the test for deceptive similarity in trademark infringement. The dispute concerned the plaintiff's registered trademark and distinctive packaging for "Glucose Biscuits" and the defendant's use of similar packaging and get-up for their biscuits marketed under the name "Glucobiscuit". The Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that the two marks, taken with their overall packaging and presentation, were deceptively similar - particularly given the class of consumers targeted, namely children and the general public, who are not expected to conduct a detailed comparison. It was held that an average consumer, possessing imperfect recollection, could easily be misled due to the visual, phonetic, and structural similarities in the competing products. Accordingly, the Hon'ble Supreme Court ruled in favour of the plaintiff and restrained the CS (Comm) No.184/2023: Ardh Sainik Canteen & Anr. V/s Bhhotpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen/ Ex.Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen: DOD: 28.10.2025 defendant from continuing use of the impugned mark. A party seeking damages/account of profits, shall give a reasonable estimate of the amounts claimed and the foundational facts/account statements in respect thereof along with any evidence, documentary and/or oral led by the parties to support such a claim. In the computation of damages, the Court may take the CS (Comm) No.184/2023: Ardh Sainik Canteen & Anr. V/s Bhhotpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen/ Ex.Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen: DOD: 28.10.2025 assistance of an expert as provided for under Rule 31 of these Rules. Further, on the aspect of damages, in case reported as, "2019:DHC:2185", tilted as, "Koninlijke Philips and Ors. V/s Amazestore & Ors.", the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has been pleased to lay down certain standards for grant of damages in following terms: xxxxx "41. Keeping in view the aforesaid, this Court is of the view that the rule of thumb that should be followed while granting damages can be summarized in a chart as under:-- # Degree of malafide conduct Proportionate award (i) First time innocent infringer Injunction (ii) First-time knowing infringer Injunction + partial costs (iii) Repeated knowing infringer Injunction + costs + which causes minor impact to partial damages the plaintiff Ardh Sainik Canteen vs Bhhotpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen on 28 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7367288/ 11 (iv) Repeated knowing infringer Injunction + costs+ which causes major impact to compensatory damages the plaintiff (v) Infringement which was Injunction + Costs + deliberate and calculated Aggravated damages (gangster/scam/mafia) + (compensatory + wilfful contempt of Court additional damages) 42. It is clarified that the above chart is illustrative and CS (Comm) No.184/2023: Ardh Sainik Canteen & Anr. V/s Bhhotpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen/ Ex.Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen: DOD: 28.10.2025 is not to be read as a statutory provision. The Courts are free to deviate from the same for good reason." Be that as it may, taking a holistic view of the matter vis-a-vis provisions as laid down under Rule 20 of the IPD Rules, 2022 and applying the ratio of law laid down by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case of "Koninlijke Philips" (supra), I am of the considered opinion that grant of damages @ Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Only) to the plaintiff would meet the ends of justice.
